Bronny on LeBron James' Lakers exit: 'He's got his own path'

Sept. 28

Bronny on LeBron James' Lakers exit: 'He's got his own path'

When LeBron James chose to leave the Los Angeles Lakers in free agency over the summer, he consulted his family on the decision to sign with the Philadelphia 76ers. But when it came to his son/teammate Bronny, much was apparently left unsaid.

"We're men of very little words when it comes to talking about business and what we're going to do and how we feel about each other. So it wasn't really much [discussion] to be honest with you," Bronny James said Monday at Lakers media day.

"He's got his own path and I got my own. He knows that I want to make a name for myself and I want to continue my career and keep growing as a player. And he knows that I want to focus on that. So he decided to do that."

LeBron and Bronny have routinely been in unique situations in league history, whether it was opening night two years ago, when the father and son entered the game together, or last year in the playoffs, where they combined to deliver a 10-0 run during a victory over the Houston Rockets. Navigating a complex free agency in which the father leaves and the son stays is another one for the books.

Tatum 'comfortable' leading new-look Celtics post-Brown trade

Jayson Tatum's one constant during his development into a star with the Boston Celtics was having Jaylen Brown as a teammate.

That partnership ended this offseason when the Celtics' front office decided to trade Brown -- the 2024 NBA Finals MVP -- to the Philadelphia 76ers in what was largely a cost-cutting move that broke up the duo most responsible for leading Boston to the 2024 NBA championship.

"The business of the NBA comes and plays a part at some point. And I've seen it in my almost 10 years in this league," Tatum said during Celtics media day on Monday. "For me it's more so being grateful for what we accomplished and what he means for this city and to this organization. Just the ups and downs in our career that we were able to grow and learn from and made us the players that we are today. So really just being thankful for those nine years."

Suns owner Ishbia says mortgage company woes won't hurt team
It's well-known at this point that billionaire Mat Ishbia's mortgage company has had a rough financial stretch.

The owner of the Phoenix Suns said Monday that will have "zero" effect on his spending habits when it comes to basketball. In fact, the 46-year-old said he's working on purchasing 14% more of the team, bringing his total to roughly 80%.

Ishbia's company -- United Wholesale Mortgage -- suffered a reported $450 million net loss in the second quarter this year, calling into question if the sizable dip would affect his basketball business. The outspoken Ishbia was adamant that nothing would change for the NBA franchise when it comes to spending on players or the fan experience.

Williamson not where he wants to be
New Orleans Pelicans forward Zion Williamson kept his answer brief when asked how he would summarize his first seven years as an NBA player.
"I'm not where I want to be," said Williamson, whom the Pelicans drafted with the No. 1 pick out of Duke in 2019. "I'm not where I need to be."

Butler indicates he is 'ahead' in his knee rehab

Nearing the eight-month mark since his right ACL surgery, Jimmy Butler III is hesitant to put a specific target date on his eventual NBA return, but he did express optimism in advance of Golden State Warriors training camp.

"I promise you I'm coming back, and it's going to be -- I think it's going to be, like, real eye-popping for everybody how I'm still going to be nice," Butler said. "Probably nicer, honestly."

Butler has only recently advanced to running, and he will be limited to light on-court individual work when the team begins practice in Hawaii on Tuesday afternoon.

It will be several weeks before Butler is expected to advance to a more rigorous stage of his rehab, and the team's lead medical decision-maker, Rick Celebrini, is known for his cautiousness in the later stages of the rehab process.

A January or February return can be considered on the optimistic side for Butler, who turned 37 earlier this month. But Butler did say that the strengthening tests on the knee indicate he is ahead of schedule.

"My numbers are staggering," Butler said. "They're off the charts. I'm ahead, so they say. So, I just know that all the work that I've been doing, whether it be at home, in L.A., in Europe, in South America, wherever the case may be, I've been doing all the right things. So, I am confident that whenever I come back, I'll be more than ready, I'll be more than healthy and I'll be a better all-around player than I was whenever I went down." -- Anthony Slater

Pistons eye "better version" of Cunningham

Detroit Pistons coach J.B. Bickerstaff has held many offseason conversations with All-NBA guard Cade Cunningham about seizing greatness and the necessary steps toward improving after last year's playoff run that stretched to Game 7 of the Eastern Conference semifinals.

Bickerstaff has guaranteed "a better version" Cunningham this season, which could be a scary sight after he averaged 23.9 points, 9.9 assists, 5.5 rebounds and 1.4 steals in 33.9 minutes during 2025-26. But Cunningham also led the East in turnovers per game after finishing with the second most in 2024-25.

"I don't have to challenge Cade, and that's why he is who he is," Bickerstaff said. "Because he's pulling. He's not being pushed."

Cunningham showed up in a fresh pair of Nike S.T. Charge "Detroit Tough" sneakers in Pistons colors. He will also receive his own signature Nike shoe, which is expected to debut during the second half of the season.

"I'm thankful to be in these shoes. I'm thankful to have the opportunity to represent my family in this way," Cunningham said. "Represent where I come from, but then to represent the city of Detroit.

"In a city like this, it's a blessing. I'm thankful for it, I don't take it for granted and I'm trying to make the most out of it." -- Eric Woodyard

Hornets waive former No. 8 pick Dillingham

The Charlotte Hornets are waiving guard Rob Dillingham, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Dillingham was traded from the Chicago Bulls on Saturday for Buddy Hield and cash. The Hornets created a $9.6 million trade exception with the move.

Dillingham, 21, appeared in 30 games for the Bulls last season, averaging 9.6 points and 2.8 assists.

SGA on chance at historic third straight MVP

At Oklahoma City Thunder media day, guard Shai Gilgeous-Alexander discussed the possibility of winning a third straight NBA MVP award and whether that's something he ponders going into this season.

"No different than any other year: Try to be the best player I can be, try to implement the things I just worked on," Gilgeous-Alexander said.

"The decision for MVP is literally 82 games away. I'm not going to win the award in the first week of the season. ... That kind of recipe for me in the past has kind of worked, and I've been fortunate to win two in a row.

"We need to be laser focused on ourselves. We need to take the lessons from that [Western Conference finals] series, for sure, and we did. But it's certainly not something that we overcorrect for, because you end up chasing your shadow, and it prevents you from being your best as you move forward."

ESPN's Summer Forecast gave Gilgeous-Alexander the fourth-best chance at the 2027 MVP, behind Victor Wembanyama, Nikola Jokic and Luka Doncic. No player has won three consecutive MVPs since Larry Bird in 1984, 1985 and 1986. -- Baxter Holmes

Doncic talks LeBron exit, Lakers "championship" ceiling
Speaking to ESPN's Brian Windhorst during Los Angeles Lakers media day, guard Luka Doncic detailed his reaction to LeBron James leaving for the Philadelphia 76ers this past summer and why he thinks a successful 2026-27 includes a Lakers run to the title:

"It was kind of sad. Playing with LeBron was amazing. There's a lot of things I learned from him. ... We all know who LeBron James is."

Shams: Duren's relationship with Pistons "has fractures"

Simmons "didn't touch a ball for a year"

During Sacramento Kings media day, guard Ben Simmons laid out the reasons he chose the Kings and why he's excited for the 2026-27 season.

"The expectations are low. I feel like that's been something on me too, so we can relate in that way," Simmons told reporters. "I think we have a chip on our shoulder."

Simmons last played in 2024-25, appearing in 51 games for the Brooklyn Nets and LA Clippers. The three-time All-Star said the time away gave him the chance to focus on "getting my body right and my mind right."

Pistons GM hasn't spoken with Duren all summer

Jalen Duren and the Detroit Pistons have a decision to make as the clock ticks closer to Oct. 1 -- the deadline to sign a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer.

For Duren, he can accept the five-year, $200 million contract that has been offered by Detroit or he can become the first player named All-NBA or All-Star to sign the qualifying offer. If he chooses the latter, Duren will hold veto power on any trade this season and be an unrestricted free agent next summer.

For the Pistons, weighing the risk of having an All-NBA player on a one-year contract and, more importantly, the likelihood he will depart next summer as a free agent is key.

There are eight projected teams that have significant cap space to sign Duren to a four-year, $189 million max contract.

"I can't control the different things that he does or his group does," Pistons president of basketball operations Trajan Langdon said at media day. "For me, it's control what we can and letting him know he is a big part of what we do."

Langdon also said he hasn't spoken with Duren all summer during Pistons media day. -- Bobby Marks

Mitchell: LeBron to Cavs made sense "for a lot of reasons"

At Cavaliers media day, Donovan Mitchell said that in his mind, he thought LeBron James would return to Cleveland because "for a lot of reasons it made sense."

"I didn't think Philly. I thought if he didn't come here, it'd be Golden State," Mitchell said.

After being swept in the Eastern Conference finals by the eventual champion New York Knicks then missing out on James in free agency, Cleveland kept its core intact. The Cavs signed Mitchell to a four-year, $273 million maximum extension and re-signed James Harden to a three-year, $97 million contract. Cleveland did make one major addition by acquiring Peyton Watson from the Denver Nuggets in a multiteam trade then signing the restricted free agent to a four-year, $88 million deal.

Speaking for the first time since their extensions, Mitchell and Harden both said their approaches to their new deals -- Mitchell signing as soon as he was eligible with Harden opting out to give Cleveland more flexibility to make moves -- reflected a team-first mindset.

"This is something that I want to do, and I want to win a championship," Harden said. "So, what does that look like? Making the team better, making the team whole to where we give ourselves a chance. By the way, you can have the best talented team, which I've been on before, and still not win.

"We waited, waited, waited until the front office called me, made sure that we got everything that we can get, and then we signed. We got a long way to go, but I love the direction and steps that we're taking here as a unit from top to bottom." -- Daniel Oyefusi

MacMahon: Thunder adjusting to roster changes
The departures of three championship-winning teammates doesn't yet feel like reality for Thunder superstar Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, who kidded that he still expected Luguentz Dort, Isaiah Joe and Aaron Wiggins to show up for Oklahoma City's team picture Monday afternoon.

"It's the business of the NBA, right?" Gilgeous-Alexander said, referring to the series of financially motivated trades. "I don't think anybody has played with all 12 guys their whole career. It sucks a little bit.

"My mind never even went to what we were going to be like on the court. It was more like the brotherhood."

As fellow OKC guard Jalen Williams added, "It's the weirdest thing ever." -- Tim MacMahon

Clippers announce Ingram has partially torn Achilles

The LA Clippers announced they found a partially torn Achilles tendon in Brandon Ingram's foot after his recent heel surgery. He will miss the start of the 2026-27 season.

Jokic: "I'm gonna sign next year"

Denver Nuggets center Nikola Jokic reiterated his commitment to the franchise at Monday's media day.

"I'm gonna sign next year," Jokic said. "If they want me."

Curry said knee is ready to go for the season

Golden State Warriors superstar guard Stephen Curry addressed the media Monday in offering positive updates on his injured knee.

"Knee's feeling great. Ready to go. No issues," Curry said. "I feel a lot stronger and understanding of what I'm dealing with."

Curry did acknowledge a "management element" but said there are currently no restrictions.

Nuggets confident in Jokic's future with franchise

Members of the Denver Nuggets' front office, general manager Jon Wallace and executive vice president of basketball Ben Tenzer addressed the media on Monday and answered questions regarding Nikola Jokic's future with the franchise. The three-time MVP didn't sign an extension this offseason.

"We feel very comfortable with the relation and trust there," Tenzer said. "We have no concerns."

LeBron: I wanted to finish my career with the Knicks
New Philadelphia 76er LeBron James said his decision came down to five teams this offseason and that he envisioned going to the New York Knicks before they won the 2026 title.

"I had visions of playing in [Madison Square] Garden and finishing my career in the Garden," James told ESPN on Monday during the 76ers' media day. "One of the best places I've ever played.

"I think it's the No. 1 arena in the world, as far as for a basketball player. But after they beat San Antonio, I was like, 'Hey, I can't.' I couldn't do it."

James and the 76ers will play the Knicks at the Garden on opening night, Oct. 20.

No update on Gary Trent Jr. investigation

Milwaukee Bucks governor Wes Edens did not provide an update on the league investigation into Gary Trent Jr.'s contract.

"I don't have any update," Edens said. "We're working with the league and fully cooperating with them. But I don't have any insight beyond that."

The NBA is looking into a potential cap-circumvention violation by the Bucks around Trent's deal this offseason.

Cronin: Blazers have "belief" in Ja Morant
Portland Trail Blazers' general manager Joe Cronin addressed why the franchise decided to trade for Ja Morant this offseason during Portland's media day on Monday.

"Just straight belief in Ja," Cronin said. "Our view of Ja as still a very high-level player.

"I'm sure there will be questions about fit, but we're very focused on talent."

Cronin also said veteran guard Jrue Holiday could play some minutes on the wing for Portland this season, while adding that Holiday and veteran guard Damian Lillard will have a positive influence on Morant.

Kerr: Rookie Lendeborg going to "play a ton"

Golden State Warriors coach Steve Kerr said during Monday's media day that he expects rookie Yaxel Lendeborg to "play a ton" this season.

"He's clearly going to play a ton," Kerr said. "He gives us the size and the versatility that we need.

"Whether he's a starter or coming off the bench, that will be determined the next couple of weeks."

Lendeborg was the No. 11 pick in the 2026 NBA draft and averaged 15.1 points per game at Michigan last season.

Embiid: 'Extremely excited' about this year's team
Philadelphia 76ers center Joel Embiid said Monday that he feels like the team finally has the right mix of players, after an offseason in which the franchise traded for Jaylen Brown and signed LeBron James to join the young guard tandem of VJ Edgecombe and Tyrese Maxey.

"It's hard to win when you get a group of guys together for one year, two years, maybe," he said. "I'm extremely excited about this team because we have the right mix of veteran leadership and younger guys. We might have some ups and downs, but we're gonna get there."

Wembanyama addresses last year's Finals loss
After leading by double digits in each of the five games in last season's NBA Finals, San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama said his memories of it will fuel the team this season.

"I couldn't imagine a better motivation," he said.

Harper addresses role for coming season
After offseason chatter about his role, San Antonio Spurs guard Dylan Harper said he'd follow the coaches' lead this season.

"Everyone has a competitive edge to them. But the biggest thing for me is whatever I can do, just like last year, to help the team win," he said. "Whatever position the coaches think is best for me to be in, that's the position I'll happily go in."

First look at LeBron in a 76ers uniform
New Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James is taking questions from reporters on Monday. Here's what he had to say when asked about his initial impressions of his team:

"Everybody is on the same page," James said. "We are all speaking the same language."

LeBron addressed his role too, saying he's open to whatever the team needs from him to win.

"Whatever they need me to do," he said. "The luxury of my game is I can do everything. ... Literally, I can do everything"

Kawhi: I was a distraction, ready to move forward
In his first public appearance with the Toronto Raptors after a controversy-filled summer, Kawhi Leonard addressed the NBA's investigation into him and his business dealings.

"I know why some of you guys came. You want to hear about the investigation. But in talking with the NBA and PA, I think the best decision is to move forward and focus on my time being a Toronto Raptor," he said. "I already was a distraction for the past 70 days and wasn't able to meet my teammates or do any of that stuff, minicamp stuff, so, moving forward, I just want to talk about the Toronto Raptors."

Haliburton: I am 100% healthy
Indiana Pacers guard Tyrese Haliburton said Monday that he is healthy and ready for the season.

"I am healthy. I am 100%," he said. "There will be no restrictions. That is not news. There is no source. I am the source. I am ready to go for the year."

Porzingis out indefinitely in blow to Warriors
Golden State Warriors big man Kristaps Porzingis is out indefinitely to open training camp with a health issue, according to the team.
In late July, Porzingis agreed to a two-year, $40 million contract with a player option on the second season to return to the Warriors.

Brown: KAT, Hart extension talks won't be a distraction
After reports surfaced last week that negotiations between the New York Knicks and center Karl-Anthony Towns had hit a stalemate, coach Mike Brown said Monday neither Towns' situation nor Hart's would linger in the locker room.

"We talk about everything [with the team]," Brown said. "We don't want to have any elephants in the room."

Hornets GM: Brandon Miller to be ready for training camp
After undergoing offseason surgery on his left shoulder, Hornets wing Brandon Miller should be a full participant in training camp and "ready to roll" for opening night, Hornets general manager Jeff Peterson said Monday.

stories.headline: Man City win at angry Anfield; Mourinho overshadows ugly Madrid win
stories.summary: Despite the pregame vitriol and ongoing scandal, it was no surprise that Man City won at Liverpool on Sunday. PLUS: Real Madrid won ugly and Mourinho got up to his old tricks after Vinicius' red card.
stories.body:
The European soccer season is back! After a three-week international break in which absolutely nothing happened -- nope, nothing at all -- we got a huge Premier League game as Man City snuck into Anfield and emerged with a 3-0 win over Liverpool that, while impressive, does little to remove the fog of anger that will follow Erling Haaland & Co. around for the rest of the season (and probably beyond).

Elsewhere in the Premier League, Man United and Tottenham battled to a 1-1 draw that did little to dispel the pressure on their managers, Michael Carrick and Roberto De Zerbi, even though Spurs should be walking away a little happier with the result. Beyond that, Arsenal got another win despite looking sloppy after the break.

Outside England, Real Madrid battled for a 1-0 win over Villarreal, a game that will be remembered as much for Jose Mourinho's all-too-familiar antics as it will for Vinícius Júnior's deserved red card. We also got talking points galore for Barcelona (can Lamine Yamal get some rest?), Bayern Munich (it's time to talk about Manuel Neuer), Paris Saint-Germain (who still haven't gotten going this season) and much, much more.

It's Monday morning, so what better time for some musings? Let's get into it.

- Man City show defiance in wake of cheating scandal, trounce Liverpool

- Late draw with Spurs shows how much trouble Carrick & Co. are in

- Arsenal fight back as Premier League resumes under cloud of City verdict

Man City seal off the outside world and do what they do best at Anfield

Their coach Enzo Maresca called it "noise," which is inappropriate when viewed from the outside. "Noise," like "rumor" and "speculation," implies some sort of trivial annoyance, not to be taken too seriously when you have a job to do.

City's guilty verdict is anything but "noise" -- it's a near-existential threat to the club. And no matter how convinced you are of their innocence and how much of the City Football Group spin you believe, if you think overturning the verdict is going to be a slam dunk, you're either a fool or badly deluded.

But from Maresca's perspective, it works. Give your fear a name -- "noise," in this case -- and then block it out. Professional athletes do this sort of stuff all the time. Control what you can control. Let others worry about what you can't. It's Psychology 101 and City nailed it, as they showed in a rousing second-half performance while winning 3-0 at Anfield.

At the same time, let's not over-egg this. City's players were booed and called cheats by the Liverpool fans (as you'd expect), but it's safe to say they've faced worse throughout their careers. Nor is it the case that the guilty verdict came out of the blue, somehow shattering their peaceful existence. They all knew it was a possibility when they joined the club, which is why several of them put specific clauses in their contract. Most of all, like most guys who play sports for a living, they express themselves best and are most comfortable on the field of play.

Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola evidently tried to channel the situation and energy of the occasion, but when you're without Dominik Szoboszlai, Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo (plus Hugo Ekitike, of course) there's only so much you can muster. They turned in a low-key first half, had a couple chances after the break and then the worm started to turn, beginning with Ryan Gravenberch's second yellow.

Was it harsh? I thought the first one was -- the second not so much, given he's stopping an attack from behind with no real attempt or opportunity to win the ball. It wasn't that long ago that English referees might treat players on a booking a little differently not wanting to "spoil the spectacle with a red card" (to use a dumb expression we used to hear regularly in the Premier League). But times change, consistency wins over discretion, and Chris Kavanagh is a paint-by-numbers referee. Gravenberch should have known better, simply put.

- VAR Review: Should Gravenberch have been sent off?

Even just before the red, at 11 vs. 11, Haaland should have put City ahead but down a man (one of Liverpool's best men on the day), this was only going to go one way. When you have a debutant in Lewis Koumas up front (and playing out of position), the ghost of Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola, who isn't Batman and at best can play Robin -- and more usually, Robin's friend, the one who rides in the trunk of the Batmobile -- there's only so much you can do.

Iraola's Liverpool remain a work-in-progress and will continue to be just that until they metabolize his football and their injured guys return. Not getting an on-loan, live body as short-term cover for Ekitike is another in the club's long list of boneheaded squad choices. As for City, they're one of the two most talented sides in the league by some distance and they showed it once more in the second half at Anfield. Sunday's result was anything but a surprise.

Real Madrid won, so why did Jose Mourinho whip out the old playbook?

And, by that, I mean why did he tantrum postgame and skip the news conference after the 1-0 win over Villarreal?

According to multiple reports in Spain, Mourinho was so angry at the officiating (and, presumably, in particular, Vinícius Júnior's red card) that he opted not to face the media because he feared he'd say something that would get him in trouble and cause him to be suspended for Real Madrid's upcoming games, with Sevilla and, especially, Barcelona the following weekend. And so, he declined to fulfil his media duties, becoming the first Real Madrid boss in 13 years to do so. (The last one? Why, it was also Mourinho, during his previous stint.)

It's the usual, familiar conspiracy trope about referees penalizing his team. As in-house media outlet Real Madrid TV helpfully pointed out, Los Blancos received five yellow cards despite committing just eight fouls, whereas Villarreal, who committed 13, got just two. (There's no point explaining it, but that's not how cautions work.)

Mourinho also fumed about the fact that Vinícius' goal was disallowed, and the Brazil international was sent off after VAR noticed that he pulled Nathan Saliba's hair in the buildup. (Actually, he didn't just pull it; he yanked it to the point that you can see the player's head snapping back.) The rules are pretty clear and why Mourinho (or, for that matter, Vinícius, who reacted with childlike incredulity and protested vehemently) doesn't seem to get this is hard to understand. (Weirdly, Mourinho didn't have a problem when VAR -- correctly -- intervened to overturn the assistant referee, ruling that Yan Diomande was onside when he scored the only goal.)

Unless, of course, you choose to be cynical and conclude that the fact that we're talking about Mourinho and refereeing conspiracies means we're not talking about another bumpy performance from Real Madrid, who struggled to break down a stubborn Villarreal. (It might have been different if Kylian Mbappé had taken his early chances, including the one that hit the post. Then again, it would have been different -- but in a bad way -- if Thibaut Courtois hadn't reached into his bag of miracles to deny Carlos Romero late.)

The uncomfortable reality is that this version of Real Madrid looks uncomfortably like that of Alvaro Arbeloa, Xabi Alonso and Carlo Ancelotti's final year. It's a side that doesn't play good football and when it wins, it does so thanks to individual exploits from its superstars (up front and Courtois on goal). And that's as much down to how this squad was constructed as it is to the manager.

When 1-1 feels like a win for Spurs and a defeat for Manchester United

Michael Carrick and Roberto De Zerbi went into this game leading the way in the Premier League sack race. The 1-1 draw probably doesn't change much for either of them, but from the bookies' perspective, it spoke volumes about which team is going in the right direction.

It's not Manchester United.

It's not just that they played the league's cellar dwellers at home and could muster just 0.06 xG for the first 62 minutes of the game. Nor is it the fact that Kobbie Mainoo and Youri Tielemans looked like two guys who met for the very first time Saturday morning, such was their lack of chemistry, on and off the ball. (When Conor Gallagher's deft touches are tearing you to shreds, you've got a problem.)

It's not even the fact that deep in injury time, hanging on to a 1-0 lead, nobody thinks it might be a good idea to shut down Sandro Tonali, who had all the time in the world to pick out Dominic Solanke, who is somehow picked up not by the bulky Harry Maguire, but rather by the Smurf-like Lisandro Martínez. Rather, it's the general sense of drift, a team that leaves you wondering what they actually do in their training sessions. Fans sense it too, which is why the team was booed at halftime as well as at the final whistle.

Solanke's goal gave Spurs a point, but even before that we saw the fight and chance creation De Zerbi craves. Even after Rodrigo Bentancur got sent off for the headbutt on Luke Shaw (who somehow got away with a yellow card after making a beeline for Bentancur and shoving him to the ground with both hands), Spurs kept going.

It's not just about showing character, it's about individuals too. Solanke and Mohammed Kudus simply give you more than Omar Marmoush and Mathys Tel. (Admittedly Solanke is a bit of a special case -- the prototypical "confidence player" -- but if De Zerbi pushes the right buttons, he's got himself a viable center forward.)

There's still a ton to work on, mind you, and Spurs are certainly not out of the woods. But if you want to talk about who's trending in the right direction and you're prepared to look beyond the final score, the answer is clearly Tottenham. Carrick can turn it around for United, of course he can, but you'd feel a lot more confident about his chances if United weren't playing midweek football -- something he has never experienced as a coach.

Quick hits

10. Barcelona rotate and stay perfect ... but did we need to see Lamine Yamal? Anthony Gordon's early goal (his first for the club) pretty much put an end to this game. The dark magic of Azulones boss Javier Bordalas rarely works when his teams are chasing the game from the second minute, and Getafe have the lowest possession stats in the league for a reason (they finished at 17%, which tells its own story). Meanwhile, Barça have eight wins out of eight in all competitions, the club's best start in 90-plus years, and they're averaging 4.25 goals per game.

Hansi Flick's side wasn't necessarily devastating Saturday, but it didn't need to be -- not when you have opponents like Zaid Romero opting to dribble in his own penalty box against three Barça players. And with the coach resting Pedri (for the first hour) and Pau Cubarsí, we saw a hybrid lineup aimed at conserving energy and managing minutes. All of which sort of makes the decision to give Yamal 90 minutes a bit surprising. It's not even mid-October yet, and he has already started 12 games this season. That's a lot for a 19-year-old, especially when (even with Raphinha injured) you have options on the bench.

9. Internazionale wrap it up quickly and efficiently against Parma, just how Cristian Chivu likes it: When you go up 3-0 within half an hour in your first game back after an international break and you're heading into a UEFA Champions League week, it's bound to bring a big smile to your coach's face. Maybe that's why Chivu was beaming on Saturday as Inter put their foot on Parma's neck early and never relented.

You're not going to get carried away given the caliber of the opposition -- there's a reason Parma fired their coach during the break -- but the performance confirmed Inter's depth up and down the lineup (Chivu rotated liberally) and the fact that no matter who's out there, the script and approach don't change. That continuity makes managing minutes so much more straightforward as we enter the most jam-packed period of the season.

8. Chelsea find their answers in midfield: one obvious, one less so... : They have issues in every area of the pitch, but midfield was the single most glaring weakness for Chelsea thus far this campaign. So the return of a fully fit Moisés Caicedo (Chelsea's best player, in my book) for his first club start of the season made all the difference in the 5-1 hammering of AFC Bournemouth.

That part was not a surprise, unlike the performance of his midfield teammate, Jordan Henderson, whose only other appearance had come in the ugly 3-0 loss at Brentford. Henderson delivered two goals (the second, a scrumptious free kick) and the easy narrative is that his experience (he's 36) and leadership (he's likeable and respected) provides exactly what Chelsea missed last season. That sounds a tad facile to me, and if we see too much of Henderson, it will likely mean things aren't going right for Xabi Alonso. But all credit to him: he proved a lot of doubters, including me, wrong on Saturday.

7. Lazio are joint-top of Serie A ... will they stay there or thereabouts? Every single indicator, except for the league table after the 3-1 win over Monza on Sunday, says "no." They've scored more than xG suggests (11 vs. 9.3) and conceded far less than xG suggests (4 vs. 8.1). Other than AC Milan, with whom they drew, they haven't faced a big side. And their keeper, Christos Mandas, is performing weekly miracles.

And yet they're playing with drive and intensity and have been Serie A's surprise package this season. Nobody (certainly not me) expected Rino Gattuso of all people to lead them to the top of the Serie A table. And lest we forget, all this is playing out a time when many fans -- furious with owner Claudio Lotito -- are boycotting home games, limiting themselves to following the team on the road. Logic suggests it won't last and Gattuso, to his credit, is the first to dampen enthusiasm. But if it did, what a story it would be...

6. Álex Baena channels his inner Ricardo Quaresma to lift Atlético Madrid at Alavés: Old-timers will remember Quaresma, the Portugal winger who regularly turned to the trivela: hitting crosses with the outside of his foot. It's not something you see often for two simple reasons: it's hard to pull off with any accuracy and most players today are competent enough to cross with their weaker foot. But that's just what Baena did delivering a peach of a ball for Cristian Romero winner in the 2-1 away win. Did he have to do it? Probably not. Was it fun to see? You bet.

The win keeps Atlético second in LaLiga and for much of the game, they were the better team (though Robin Le Normand reminded us why he's not top of Diego Simeone's Christmas card list, and they got help when Ángel Pérez got himself sent off for a demented tackle on Johnny Cardoso). Oh, and Julián Álvarez is reportedly switching agents following his botched summer move. Atlético fans will be hoping it helps purge all the venom of the last transfer window.

5. SC Freiburg are also top of the Bundesliga and it's unlikely to last, so enjoy it while you can: In some ways, their ascent into first place (after the 2-1 short-handed win over Schalke on Sunday) is more remarkable than Lazio's, though in some ways, it isn't. They've come to epitomize the plucky underdog "community" club standing up to the powerhouses in recent seasons (they finished seventh and fifth) and, of course, they reached the Europa League final last year, but few would have expected them to start the campaign with four wins in five, especially after a summer in which they lost Johan Manzambi and keeper Noah Atubolu to summer transfers.

So what's the special sauce here then? Continuity, for one. The legendary Christian Streich left after 12 seasons in 2024, but Julian Schuster, his former assistant, has kept the ball rolling. Igor Matanovic has come into his own as a center forward, and the back line is as stingy as ever. But -- and I hate to rain on the parade here -- they've also had a "friendly" schedule (four of their games have been against the bottom six clubs) and ridden their luck a little bit. They'll come back to Earth, but the way the season shapes up in the Bundesliga, a Champions League place is certainly not out of the question.

4. Paris Saint-Germain are maybe not as deep as we think: Take it with a grain of salt, of course, because the first outing after an international break (especially this unprecedented three-week version) is always a bit screwy. But PSG's 3-1 win over Le Mans on Saturday was nowhere near as comfortable as it looked. Paris Saint-Germain rotated heavily, but a number of understudies (from Lucas Hernández and Illia Zabarnyi at the back, to Dro Fernández in midfield to Mika Godts, making his first start, out wide) didn't exactly seize the day.

In fact, with half an hour to go, it was 1-1 and PSG were facing the very real possibility of dropping points for the fourth time in six Ligue 1 games. Luis Enrique sent on the cavalry in the form of Vitinha, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Fabián Ruiz, and the European champions eventually changed it around. But Saturday night leaves them with plenty food for thought ahead of their trip to face Manchester City in the Champions League this midweek.

3. Arsenal look sloppy in comeback home win over Leeds United: Mikel Arteta will hope it's just classic postbreak rust. At the hour mark on Saturday, Arsenal were a goal down at home and looking awkward and tame. They had put together 0.46 xG (to Leeds' 0.60) and offered James Justin a veritable highway for the visitors' opener (blame Noni Madueke for that one).

Goals from Riccardo Calafiori (with a little help from James Trafford) and substitute Bruno Guimarães turned it around to deliver the 2-1 win. But that first hour was rough, and while a lot of credit has to go to Daniel Farke's side, you expect more composure from Arsenal at home. With Declan Rice starting slowly (before reaching devastating levels after the break) and Myles Lewis-Skelly stymied, you can't help but wonder about Martín Zubimendi. A year ago, he was seen as the missing piece of the puzzle; now, despite being good enough to feature in three of four games over the break for world champions Spain, he's a guy who has started one game for Arsenal since May 1.

2. Juventus squander chances as their manager glitches (again): Let's not overcomplicate this. Juventus are far from perfect (they're not even particularly good), but they're not the mess some make them out to be. Sunday's 1-1 draw with Cagliari was a result of horrendous finishing (gee, who could have expected that when your strikers are Nick Woltemade and Randal Kolo Muani?) but based on performance, they deserved the three points.

That matters, and it matters that they're doing it without their first-choice midfield (Manuel Locatelli and Kephren Thuram) and their best player (Kenan Yildiz). Strip those pieces out of any team and see how much fun it is. Manager Luciano Spalletti is doing the best he can on the pitch; off the pitch, though, he can do better. Getting yourself sent off at full time for clashing with the opposing coach is pointless, especially when it's over such a banal point. Spalletti says all he did was congratulate his opposite number for "being good at time-wasting" and when Fabio Pisacane said "what time-wasting?" things got needlessly heated. Juve don't need Spalletti getting involved in this nonsense, they need him to do what he does best.

1. Bayern Munich, we need to talk about Manu... : As in Manuel Neuer, who got caught on the ball conceding the opener away to FC Augsburg in Saturday's 2-2 draw (after just 8.4 seconds no less, the fastest goal in the history of the Bundesliga). He wasn't great on the second goal either, pushing the ball into the path of Rodrigo Ribeiro. For Bayern, those are two points dropped in an away derby that they otherwise dominated, as evidenced by the 4.96 xG, 30 shots on goal and seven big chances created.

Neuer is 40 years old and one of the greatest -- some might say THE greatest -- keepers in Bundesliga history. His ability on the ball, coupled with his prowess between the sticks, made him unique; his character and intensity made him a leader. And truth be told, even when he was among the best in the world, he would make the occasional howler (something his critics blamed on overconfidence). The difference is that the lag time between his major errors is getting shorter and shorter. We saw at the FIFA World Cup as well, when he unretired for an improbable swan song that turned out to be just that. Bayern have been planning for the post-Neuer era for years (remember Alexander Nübel?) and it is starting to feel as if he's still around due to an unwillingness to have tough conversations rather than a belief that he should still be No. 1.

stories.headline: When can Kimi Antonelli win the F1 title? Earliest date, points needed and remaining races
stories.summary: Kimi Antonelli took another big step towards his first world title after outscoring his two closest championship rivals, George Russell and Lewis Hamilton, at the Singapore Grand Prix.
stories.body:
Kimi Antonelli took another big step towards his first world title after outscoring his two closest championship rivals, George Russell and Lewis Hamilton, at the Singapore Grand Prix.

The 20-year-old, who has the potential to set a new record for the youngest Formula 1 champion this year, now leads Mercedes teammate Russell by 102 points in the standings with a maximum of 150 points still up for grabs.

The substantial lead means he could be crowned champion as early as Oct. 24 at the U.S. Grand Prix in Austin, but the maths around that calculation are slightly complicated by question marks over the final two races of the season. The grands prix in Qatar and Abu Dhabi are currently scheduled to go ahead on Nov. 29 and Dec. 6, but escalations in the war between the United States and Iran have the potential to force the cancellation of both rounds.

F1 has put a contingency plan in place to hold a single round at Imola if Qatar and Abu Dhabi are cancelled, but doing so would cut the championship short by one round and mean only 125 points are available to any single driver before the end of the year. Such a scenario would change the maths around the championship fight, making it easier for Antonelli to be crowned champion in Austin.

- 'Chucky' Verstappen is back. Luckily for Antonelli and Mercedes, it's too late

- Max Verstappen takes back-to-back wins with dominant drive at Singapore GP

- Lewis Hamilton calls Singapore GP strategy 'painful lesson' after Ferrari apology

Alongside Russell and Hamilton, Max Verstappen, Charles Leclerc and Lando Norris are still mathematically in contention for this year's championship, although the incredibly slim hopes of Leclerc and Norris would be snuffed out entirely by the cancellation of the races in the Middle East.

What does Antonelli need to do to be crowned champion in Austin?
Assuming the final two races go ahead as planned, Antonelli's chances of clinching the title in Austin remain relatively slim. The Mercedes driver would need to win in Texas, with his teammate Russell finishing ninth or lower and Hamilton finishing fifth or lower.

Such a scenario would put Antonelli 125 points ahead of Russell with 125 points remaining, but even if Antonelli failed to score another point and Russell won all the remaining rounds after Austin, Antonelli would still be crowned champion on countback of race victories (by that stage Antonelli would be on nine and Russell on three with five races remaining).

If the championship is shortened by the season ending in Imola rather than Abu Dhabi, Antonelli would only need to leave Austin with a lead of 100 points over his rivals.

Such a scenario would result in the following permutations:

If Antonelli wins in Austin he would be crowned champion regardless of where the others finish.
If Antonelli finishes second, he would be crowned champion if Russell doesn't win the race.
If Antonelli finishes third, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes off the podium.
If Antonelli finishes fourth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes behind him and Hamilton does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes fifth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes fourth or lower and Hamilton does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes sixth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes fifth or lower and Hamilton does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes seventh, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes sixth or lower and Hamilton does not finish in the top two.
If Antonelli finishes eighth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes seventh or lower, Hamilton does not finish in the top two and Verstappen does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes ninth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes eighth or lower, Hamilton does not finish in the top three and Verstappen does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes tenth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes ninth or lower, Hamilton does not finish in the top three and Verstappen does not win the race.
If Antonelli fails to score, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes ninth or lower, Hamilton finishes fifth or lower and Verstappen does not win the race.

What's the minimum Antonelli needs to do be crowned champion?
Another way to look at the championship is the minimum amount of points Antonelli needs to score over the remaining rounds to secure the title regardless of what other drivers achieve. Assuming Qatar and Abu Dhabi go ahead, he needs 49 points over the remaining rounds, which could be achieved with as little as five sixth place finishes and one fifth place finish over the rest of the season.

If only five races remain, Antonelli would need just 24 points to secure the title, which would be attainable with two seventh place finishes and three eighth place finishes at the remaining rounds.

stories.headline: 'Disjointed' WNBA causing WNBL scheduling issues
stories.summary: One of the WNBL's star players has labelled an overlap between the WNBA and Australia's domestic season "hard" ahead of the league's tip-off on Thursday.
stories.body:
The WNBL is considering pushing back the start of next season's competition, with several big-name players expected to miss the opening games of the upcoming campaign.

Reigning league MVP Isobel Borlase (Bendigo), Opal Miela Sowah (Townsville) and import Madina Okot (Tasmania) will not feature in at least the opening two weekends of the Australian competition when it begins on Thursday.

They will instead be competing in the WNBA finals, where Borlase and Okot are looking to deliver the Atlanta Dream their first title, while Sowah is part of the Golden State Valkyries' fairytale run.

With the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup held in September, the American competition stopped for 17 days and subsequently ended later than scheduled.

This means the league has directly clashed with the start of the WNBL campaign.

Making matters worse, in 2027 the WNBA is expanding the number of regular-season games, meaning the competition will run until November.

With the prospect of WNBL imports and Australian Opals still playing overseas, there is a huge risk that marquee players could miss the opening month of the league if it starts in October, as it does this season.

"We're always considering what the best possible situation is for not only Australians but other international players that want to play in the WNBL," the league's chief operating officer Justin Nelson told AAP.

"Is there the prospect of maybe starting a little bit later? The short answer is yes.

"But how much we may or may not move is still to be seen."

Adelaide Lightning coach Aja Parham-Ammar is waiting to see how Opal Steph Talbot pulls up after her Las Vegas Aces were knocked out of the WNBA semi-finals on Saturday (AEDT).

The Lightning play the Sydney Flames on Sunday, but of bigger concern beyond whether she will play is that Talbot has missed all of the team's pre-season.

"It (not having Talbot) can be disruptive or disjointed a bit, but you've got to be grateful that you have talent that's playing at the highest level," the coach told AAP.

"It (moving the season back) is definitely a conversation to be had. With WNBA being the top league, you want to be able to bring that top talent over and not create issues with recruiting."

Also in a sticky situation are the Geelong Venom, who have recruited towering superstar Han Xu.

The Chinese national was part of the New York Liberty side that lost the semi-final against Atlanta, and it is unclear if she will feature in the WNBL season opener against the Tasmania Jewels on Thursday.

Regardless, star guard Bec Cole says the Venom will back themselves to win.

"We can still beat teams without Han, and then (when Geelong) bring her in there'll be an adjustment period because she's going to be a big facet of what we do," Cole told AAP.

"It is hard, and we are a new team, but that's just the game of basketball, and we're all professional."

stories.headline: Ranking every AFL free agent by the impact they'll have at their new club
stories.summary: The 2026 AFL free agency period is now complete. We've ranked every move that has been made, factoring in positional needs and their likely impact for season 2027.
stories.body:
The 2026 AFL free agency period is now complete, with seven players finding new clubs either as restricted or unrestricted free agents.

We've ranked every move that has been made, factoring in positional needs and their likely impact for season 2027 (not the rest of their career). So, who will be the biggest needle mover of the bunch in the immediate future?

7. Kieren Briggs
This is absolutely no criticism of Kieren Briggs, but there really aren't many players in the competition (if any) that could be dropped into the Tigers in 2027 and be serious needle movers. Remember, Richmond has won just 10 games across the last three seasons and is widely expected to finish in the bottom four once again next year. Tigers skipper Toby Nankervis will remain the club's primary ruck in the immediate future, but the arrival of Briggs will allow for a new-look one-two punch. The former Giant is one of the best hitout-to-advantage rucks in the game and an elite clearance winner. At 27 years of age, and with Nankervis now 32, Briggs' impact will likely be felt in the years beyond 2027.

6. Jordon Butts
Key defensive stocks have been a concern for the Bulldogs in recent years, so the signing of Jordon Butts will be a welcomed addition for the club. Butts makes the move after eight seasons and 94 games with the Crows, but he's managed just 10 and nine games in 2025 and 2026. Throughout different parts of the last couple of years, he's struggled with unlucky injuries; in 2025 it was a collapsed lung, and this year he battled concussion and a fractured foot. With the continued strong form of Josh Worrell and Mark Keane, and emergence of Josh Borlase at the Crows, a move to the Bulldogs makes sense for both the 26-year-old Butts and the Dogs.

5. Joel Amartey
The Blues landed key forward support for Harry McKay in the form of Joel Amartey, who crosses from the Swans as an unrestricted free agent. It's a shrewd acquisition for Carlton, and the club will be hopeful he can be an upgrade on both Brodie Kemp and Mitch McGovern. Amartey is coming off a season at Sydney in which he booted 28 goals from 15 games and averaged three marks per game. In 2024 he enjoyed a career-best 43-goal campaign, including a bag of nine against the Crows. Amartey is just 27 years of age and should only really be coming into his prime as a key position player in the AFL. Could surprise a few in 2027.

4. Toby Greene
Another year, another major coup for the Cats. Is anyone surprised?! Former Giants captain Toby Greene joins Geelong as an unrestricted free agent while GWS has to make do with second-round compensation. We all know Greene has been a high-impact player throughout his 15-year career and he will add a whole new dynamic to the Cats' forward line, one that features former Giants teammate and close friend Jeremy Cameron. In 2026, Greene kicked 34 goals -- his lowest return in a season since his injury-interrupted 2020 campaign -- but did amass over 20 disposals per game. If anyone wanted to argue he deserves the top spot on this list I wouldn't scoff, but it's not as if the Cats had trouble scoring in 2026...

3. Ben King
It may have been a move that surprised few, but it's one -- along with the signing of Zach Merrett, of course -- that will have Hawks fans believing a premiership is possible in 2027. For a fair chunk of the 2026 season, King looked to be the Coleman Medal winner. Gold Coast's capitulation didn't help his chances, though he still finished the home and away season with 60 goals to his name -- the third consecutive year he's managed 55+ goals. King will partner veteran Jack Gunston and dynamo Nick Watson in what now looks to be one of the most dangerous forward lines in the game.

2. Lachie Neale
The Lachie Neale-Brisbane Lions era is over, with the two-time Brownlow Medal winner joining Collingwood as an unrestricted free agent and partnering reigning Brownlow winner Nick Daicos in a new-look Magpies midfield. Neale might be 33 years of age and on the downturn of his decorated career, but he still averaged 29 disposals, 12.5 contested possessions, and six clearances per outing in 2026 and figures to be a major contributor next season in a Collingwood engine room that's often lacked depth and firepower. Even if the Magpies receive 80-85% of this season's production from Neale, he'll be difficult to top as the most impactful free agent of the year.

1. Zak Butters
The most sought after man in football made the decision to sign with the Bulldogs during free agency. Former Power star Zak Butters joins the club as a top five player in the game, and at age 26, you can certainly make the argument he's only at the beginning of his prime. Butters will partner Western Bulldogs skipper Marcus Bontempelli and Ed Richards in what's easily the most impressive and dynamic three-pronged midfield in the competition. He offers a real point of difference, too, with his electric pace and the ability to break lines two eye-catching features that have seen him ascend to footy superstardom.

stories.headline: Denkey's double sparks Cincinnati to win over Atlanta
stories.summary: Kevin Denkey scored two goals after a scoreless first half and FC Cincinnati snapped a six-match winless streak with a 3-1 victory over Atlanta United on Saturday night.
stories.body:
ATLANTA -- Kevin Denkey scored two goals after a scoreless first half and FC Cincinnati snapped a six-match winless streak with a 3-1 victory over Atlanta United on Saturday night.

Denkey scored in the 52nd minute to give Cincinnati (9-9-9) a 1-0 lead. Tom Barlow and David Douděra had assists.

Miguel Almirón used passes from Breel Embolo and Tomás Jacob to score his fifth goal and tie it 1-all in the 69th minute.

Kyle Smith set up Tom Barlow for the go-ahead goal in the 84th minute, and Denkey scored in the seventh minute of stoppage time to wrap up the victory.

Denkey has 16 goals on the season, one more than he had last year in his first 29 league appearances.

Barlow has eight goals and four assists this season - both career highs through 200 career matches.

Evan Louro turned away five shots in his third start in goal this season for Cincinnati and the eighth of his career.

Lucas Hoyos had one save for Atlanta United (7-15-6) in his first MLS campaign.

Cincinnati improves to 2-7-6 on the road while ending an 0-3-3 stretch overall. The club beat Atlanta United 2-0 at home in the season opener to complete the sweep.

Atlanta United saw a three-match unbeaten run end while falling to 4-8-2 at home.

Up next Cincinnati: Hosts New England Revolution on Wednesday.

Atlanta: At CF Montreal on Wednesday.

stories.headline: New Zealand Rugby launches legal action against ARLC over 'Chiefs' name
stories.summary: The battle over the use of the "Chiefs" name is headed to the New Zealand High Court after New Zealand Rugby launched legal action against the Australian Rugby League Commission.
stories.body:
The battle over the use of the "Chiefs" name is headed to the New Zealand High Court after New Zealand Rugby launched legal action against the Australian Rugby League Commission.

NZR on Thursday said it had been left with no choice but to launch legal proceedings against the ARLC, who has sought to adopt the name for its Papua New Guinea expansion franchise.

The PNG Chiefs are due to join the NRL in 2028 and have already signed a raft of players, including code-hoppers Zac Lomaz and Joey Manu, but they may yet have to undergo a chanGe of name if NZR gets its way.

The Chiefs' Super Rugby franchise has existed since 1996, with NZR claiming the introduction of the PNG Chiefs would result in "significant confusion and damage" should they be allowed to compete under the name from 2028.

"New Zealand Rugby (NZR) has today moved to protect the Chiefs brand and is filing proceedings in the High Court of New Zealand against the decision by the Australian Rugby League Commission (ARLC) to launch a new NRL side using "Chiefs" in its name," an NZR statement read.  

"NZR is seeking both an interim and final injunction which stops the use of the names 'PNG Chiefs', 'Chiefs' or any other similar names in New Zealand.   

"The Chiefs have competed as a professional rugby team in Super Rugby since 1996 and over those 30 years, have built a strong identity and fanbase across New Zealand, Australia and internationally.  

"In New Zealand, NZR owns both the trademark rights for the word Chiefs and the Chiefs logo and since 1998, NZR has also held trademark protection for the Chiefs logo in Australia."

NZR claims it had tried to engage with the ARLC in an attempt to find a resolution, yet the commission was now intent on proceeding with the official launch of the PNG Chiefs on Oct. 21.

"For 30 years the Chiefs and their players have built an incredibly strong identity that is widely recognised and loved by fans," NZR chief executive Steve Lancaster said. "We have raised our concerns with the ARLC directly and consistently over the last year in attempting to find a resolution. We now have a responsibility to protect the Chiefs brand.   

"We want to be absolutely clear, this is not about rugby league's growth in the Pacific. We welcome the development of the Pacific region through sport and the passion that the people of Papua New Guinea have for both rugby and rugby league."  

The Chiefs won two Super Rugby titles in back-to-back seasons in 2012 and 2013, and were runners-up in Super Rugby Pacific this season after suffering a crushing defeat by the Hurricanes in the decider.

The Hamilton-based team has produced countless All Blacks since its inception, with Saturday's run-on team to face the Wallabies featuring six players from the franchise.

"Here in New Zealand, when people hear 'the Chiefs', they think of this club and this region. The identity carries significant cultural meaning and connection to the region and its people, we know it means a great deal to our players and coaches past and present, fans and supporters here and around the world," Chiefs CEO Simon Graafhuis said.   

"Teams in different sports and markets can exist alongside one another with the same name, but the issue here is the similarity of our sports competing in the same market, for the same fans, in overlapping windows."  

However, ARLC executive chairman Peter V'Landys later issued a stinging rebuke, insisting he would vigorously defend PNG's right to use the Chiefs as its team name.

"The hypocrisy is mind-blowing, considering the Auckland Blues in 1996 used the NSW Blues name without any consultation or approval. The NSW Blues had been the Blues for in excess of 50 years before that," he said.

"Rugby union is obviously feeling threatened by rugby league in New Zealand, with sell-outs at most rugby league games."

No date has yet been slated for the hearing in New Zealand's High Court.
